current.text: He is a projected starter in Orlando's lineup with Bane, Franz Wagner, Banchero and Carter. That five was very good when it played together.
Orlando has a new head coach, Sean Sweeney, so roles may change.
Orlando is 2.5 million USD under the second apron and will likely have to choose between keeping Suggs and keeping Black.
One expert thinks Suggs is the likely trade sacrifice so Orlando can keep Black.
He shot badly in the playoffs: under 30% from the field and in the low 20s from three.
Experts rate him a top 70 to 80 player per game when healthy. They say drafts have him far too low and he is worth the shot at his price.
He sits in tier 8 at both guard spots. If he plays 65 to 70 games, he would rank ahead of nearly everyone in that tier.
Plan for him to miss about 20 games this season.
He went for 9 USD in an expert auction mock draft.
He reached his career-high assists last season without a healthy summer. A healthy offseason could unlock another level.
Orlando is projected for 47 or 48 wins and the 6th seed.

durable.text: He is injury prone. His physical, all-out style of play wears his body down.
Availability is his main issue. He cannot be trusted to stay healthy.
His three-point shooting is streaky. When it is on, he shoots about six threes a game.
Steals are his standout category, far above the top 250 pool.

note: Suggs is a cheap per-game value. Yahoo prices him at 5 USD, ESPN at 0 USD, and he went for 1 USD in our league last season. Experts see a top 70 to 80 player per game, and he went for 9 USD in an expert mock. His steals, threes and assists help any build, but his FG% and turnovers lean negative. He has played 57 and 35 games the last two seasons, so in a 12-team league he works best as a 3 to 6 USD guard with a plan for missed games. Early in the season, watch his health and whether Orlando trades him to keep Black under the second apron.
